subject: DI01000021

intro_text.en: Unit 1 of Mathematics-I: determinants of the second and third order evaluated by minors and cofactors (no properties, exactly as the syllabus asks), their use in Cramer's rule, the area of a triangle and the collinearity test; then the function as a one-output machine with domain, codomain, range, standard graphs, even/odd and piecewise rules; then the logarithm as a function, its domain and graph, the laws of logarithm and their numericals. Twenty-five fully solved numericals, every one linked to a card.

body.en:
Definition

A determinant is a single number calculated from a square array of numbers. For a second-order determinant the array has two rows and two columns:

|a b; c d| = ad − bc - the product of the main diagonal minus the product of the other diagonal.

Notation that matters

  • Vertical bars mean value: |3 5; 2 4| = 2. Brackets [3 5; 2 4] mean a matrix, which is an array, not a number.
  • The determinant of matrix A is written |A| or det(A).
  • Read it as [a b; c d] in the same layout as the array: a and d are on the main diagonal (top-left to bottom-right).

Worked example

|3 5; 2 4| = (3)(4) − (5)(2) = 12 − 10 = 2.

Is |2 4; 1 2| zero?

Yes: (2)(2) − (4)(1) = 0. Rows (and columns) are proportional, which is exactly what a zero determinant signals.

h.en: 1.2 Second-order determinants with a variable, and what a zero says

body.en:
Definition

The entries may be expressions, so the determinant becomes an equation in x. Solve it exactly as a quadratic once the expansion is done.

Worked example

Find x if |x 2; 3 x| = 10. Expand: x·x − 2·3 = 10 → x² − 6 = 10 → x² = 16 → x = 4 or x = −4.

Reading a zero determinant

DeterminantMeaning for two equations in x and y
D ≠ 0Unique solution - the two lines cross once
D = 0 but Dx or Dy ≠ 0No solution - the lines are parallel
D = 0 and Dx = Dy = 0Infinitely many solutions - the same line twice

Common mistake / conditions

Do not write x² = 16 and answer x = 4 only. A squared equation has two roots; in a geometry question you may reject the negative one, but you must say so.

Definition

A third-order determinant is expanded into three second-order determinants, with alternating signs + − + along the first row:

|a₁ b₁ c₁; a₂ b₂ c₂; a₃ b₃ c₃| = a₁(b₂c₃ − b₃c₂) − b₁(a₂c₃ − a₃c₂) + c₁(a₂b₃ − a₃b₂)

The three steps

  1. Cover the row and column of the entry you are multiplying.
  2. Write the 2×2 determinant that is left (this is the minor).
  3. Attach the sign from the pattern + − + / − + − / + − + and add the three terms.

Worked example

|1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 10| = 1(5×10 − 6×8) − 2(4×10 − 6×7) + 3(4×8 − 5×7) = 1(2) − 2(−2) + 3(−3) = 2 + 4 − 9 = −3.

Common mistake / conditions

The signs belong to the position, not to the entry. If b₁ is already negative, its term is −(−3)(minor) = +3(minor). Write the sign in brackets before substituting.

Definition

The minor Mᵢⱼ of an entry is the 2×2 determinant left after deleting row i and column j. The cofactor is the same number with the positional sign:

Cᵢⱼ = (−1)^(i+j) Mᵢⱼ

The sign board

column 1column 2column 3
row 1+−+
row 2−+−
row 3+−+

Worked idea

For A = [2 3 1; 4 0 5; 1 2 3], the minor of the 4 (row 2, column 1) is |3 1; 2 3| = 9 − 2 = 7, and its cofactor is −7 because position (2, 1) carries a minus.

Why both names exist

The determinant equals the sum a₁₁C₁₁ + a₁₂C₁₂ + a₁₃C₁₃ along any row or column. Cofactors are also the raw material of the adjoint and the inverse in later semesters.

h.en: 2.3 Choosing the easiest row, and the Sarrus shortcut

body.en:
Definition

Because any row or column may be used, choose the one with the most zeros: every zero kills a whole 2×2 determinant and saves arithmetic.

Worked example

|2 −1 3; 0 4 −2; 5 1 0| - the second row has a zero, but the third column has one too. Expanding along the third column: 3(0×1 − 4×5) − (−2)(2×1 − (−1)×5) + 0 = −60 + 2(7) = −46.

Sarrus rule (third order only)

Copy the first two columns to the right and add the three down-right diagonals, then subtract the three down-left diagonals. It is a check, not a substitute for the expansion: for the matrix above Sarrus gives 0 + (−10) + 0 − (60 + 0 + 0) = −46 ✓.

Conditions

Sarrus works only for 3×3. Never try it on a 4×4 - the diagonal trick does not generalise.

Definition

For a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂, build three determinants:

D = |a₁ b₁; a₂ b₂|, Dx = |c₁ b₁; c₂ b₂|, Dy = |a₁ c₁; a₂ c₂|

then x = Dx/D and y = Dy/D, provided D ≠ 0.

Worked example

2x + 3y = 12, x − y = 1. D = (2)(−1) − (3)(1) = −5; Dx = (12)(−1) − (3)(1) = −15; Dy = (2)(1) − (12)(1) = −10. So x = 3, y = 2.

Common mistake / conditions

The column that is replaced is the one of the variable you are finding: for Dx replace the x-column (the first) by the constants. Swapping the wrong column gives the other variable's value and is the most common error in this question.

Definition

Three equations in x, y, z need four determinants: D, Dx, Dy, Dz, each third order. Replace one column of the coefficient determinant by the constants each time.

Worked example

x + y + z = 6, x − y + z = 2, 2x + y − z = 1. Expanding the coefficient determinant by the first row gives D = 6; then Dx = 6, Dy = 12, Dz = 18, so x = 1, y = 2, z = 3 - which checks in all three equations.

Practical advice

Cramer is long for 3×3. Use it when the question asks for determinants, and use elimination when it only asks for the solution. Either way the check is the same: substitute all three values into all three equations.

h.en: 3.3 Area of a triangle and the collinearity test

body.en:
Formula

For vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₃, y₃):

Area = ½ |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|, equal to ½ |det| of the 3×3 determinant with a final column of 1s.

Worked example

(1, 2), (4, 6), (7, 2): ½|1(6 − 2) + 4(2 − 2) + 7(2 − 6)| = ½|4 + 0 − 28| = 12 square units.

Collinearity

If the three points lie on one line the triangle has no area, so the determinant is zero. That single test answers every "show that the points are collinear" question - and its converse is a fast check of your own answer.

h.en: 4.1 Definition, notation, domain, codomain and range

body.en:
Definition

A function f from set A to set B assigns exactly one element of B to every element of A. Written f : A → B, y = f(x).

The four words

WordMeaningExample for f(x) = x², A = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2}
DomainEverything you may put in{−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} (or all real x)
CodomainThe set you are mapping intothe real numbers
RangeWhat actually comes out{0, 1, 4}
ImageOutput for one particular inputf(2) = 4

One input, one output

The rule "one value in, exactly one value out" is what makes it a function. y² = x is not a function of x, because x = 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2. On a graph, a vertical line may meet a function's curve only once.

Definition

The domain is restricted by two things only at this level: a denominator may not be zero, and an even root may not be negative.

Rules

FunctionRestrictionDomain
1/(x − 3)x − 3 ≠ 0all real x except 3
√(x − 2)x − 2 ≥ 0x ≥ 2, that is [2, ∞)
1/√(x − 2)x − 2 > 0x > 2
log xx > 0(0, ∞)
polynomialnoneall real x

Common mistake / conditions

In 1/√(x − 2) the root already forbids negatives, and the denominator forbids zero, so the endpoint 2 is excluded (>, not ≥). One word changes the whole answer - write the condition before the interval.

Definition

Five shapes cover almost every question in this unit. Knowing the shape lets you read the domain and range straight off the picture.

FunctionRuleShapeRange (a > 0)
Constanty = chorizontal line{c}
Lineary = mx + cstraight lineall real y
Quadraticy = ax² + bx + cparabolay ≥ vertex value
Exponentialy = aˣalways rising, asymptotic to the x-axisy > 0
Logarithmicy = logₐ xmirror of the exponentialall real y

Reading a graph

  1. Domain: project the curve onto the x-axis.
  2. Range: project it onto the y-axis.
  3. A hole or a vertical asymptote is a value the function never takes - exclude it.

Worked example

For y = x² − 4x + 7, completing the square gives y = (x − 2)² + 3, so the range is y ≥ 3 with the vertex at (2, 3).

Definition

A function is even if f(−x) = f(x) (symmetric about the y-axis) and odd if f(−x) = −f(x) (symmetric about the origin). A piecewise function uses a different rule on different parts of its domain.

Test procedure

  1. Replace every x by −x.
  2. Simplify and compare with f(x) and −f(x).
  3. Equal to f(x): even. Equal to −f(x): odd. Neither: neither - and say so.

Worked examples

f(x) = x³ − x: f(−x) = −x³ + x = −(x³ − x) → odd. g(x) = x² + 1: g(−x) = x² + 1 = g(x) → even. h(x) = x² + x: h(−x) = x² − x, which is neither → neither.

For f(x) = x + 1 when x < 0 and f(x) = x² when x ≥ 0: f(−2) = −1 and f(3) = 9. Choose the rule by the input, never by the answer.

h.en: 5.1 Definition: the inverse of the exponential

body.en:
Definition

y = logₐ x ⇔ aʸ = x, where a > 0, a ≠ 1 and x > 0. The logarithm answers the question "to what power must the base be raised?"

The two directions

Logarithm formExponential formRead as
log₂ 32 = 52⁵ = 322 to the power 5 is 32
log₅ 1 = 05⁰ = 1any base to the power 0 is 1
log₃ (1/27) = −33⁻³ = 1/27a negative logarithm means a fraction
log₁₀ 1000 = 310³ = 1000common logarithm

Two values worth memorising

logₐ 1 = 0 and logₐ a = 1. Both follow from the definition and both are used to simplify answers.

Common mistake / conditions

The base is written small and low: logₐ x. log 100 with no base means base 10, and ln x means base e ≈ 2.718. Never take the log of a negative number or of zero - the domain is x > 0.

Definition

Because aˣ is always positive, only positive numbers have logarithms: the domain of logₐ x is (0, ∞). The output can be any real number, so the range is (−∞, ∞).

The mirror

Swap x and y in y = aˣ and you get x = aʸ, that is y = logₐ x. The two graphs are reflections of each other in the line y = x. The exponential has a horizontal asymptote y = 0; the logarithm has a vertical asymptote x = 0 and crosses the x-axis at (1, 0).

Shape warnings

  • a > 1: the curve rises slowly; log₁₀ 1000 = 3 while log₁₀ 10 = 1.
  • 0 < a < 1: the curve falls - a decreasing logarithm.
  • The curve never touches x = 0; it dives without reaching it.

Application

Logarithms turn multiplication into addition, which is why they appear wherever a quantity grows by a fixed factor - sound level, earthquake magnitude, pH, and the number of digits of a large power.

Definition

log x (base 10) is used in engineering data tables; ln x (base e) is used in calculus and in growth/decay formulae. Both obey the same laws - only the base changes.

Useful numbers

QuantityValueWhy it is useful
log₁₀ 20.3010halving and doubling times
log₁₀ 30.4771powers of 3
log₁₀ e0.4343convert ln to log
ln 20.6931half-life and doubling time
ln 102.3026convert log to ln

Converting

ln x = 2.3026 log x and log x = 0.4343 ln x. The conversion is just the change of base formula with base e, which appears in the next section.

Common mistake / conditions

log 2 + log 3 = log 6, but log 2 × log 3 is not log 6 - the laws apply to the sum of logs, not to their product. Keep the operation and the law matched.

Definition

For a > 0, a ≠ 1 and positive x, y:

LawStatementExample
Productlogₐ(xy) = logₐ x + logₐ ylog 6 = log 2 + log 3
Quotientlogₐ(x/y) = logₐ x − logₐ ylog 1.5 = log 3 − log 2
Powerlogₐ(xⁿ) = n logₐ xlog 8 = 3 log 2

Why they hold

Write x = aᵐ and y = aⁿ. Then xy = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, so logₐ(xy) = m + n = logₐ x + logₐ y. The laws are consequences of the index laws - not new rules to memorise.

Using them in both directions

Expand: log(3x²/y) = log 3 + 2 log x − log y. Condense: 2 log 3 + log 4 − log 6 = log(9 × 4 / 6) = log 6. Exams ask for both directions, so practise both.

h.en: 6.2 Change of base and the derived laws

body.en:
Definition

logₐ x = log_b x / log_b a. Choosing b = 10 turns any base into a calculator evaluation; choosing b = x gives logₐ x · log_x a = 1.

Derived results

ResultHow it follows
logₐ(1/x) = −logₐ xpower law with n = −1
logₐ b = 1 / log_b achange of base, then simplify
logₐ a = 1 and logₐ 1 = 0definition
a^(logₐ x) = xthe two operations undo each other

Worked example

log₄ 8 = log 8 / log 4 = 3 log 2 / 2 log 2 = 3/2 = 1.5. The powers of 2 cancel, so no calculator is needed - always look for a common base first.

Common mistake / conditions

log(x + y) is not log x + log y, and (log x)² is not 2 log x. The laws act on products, quotients and powers - nothing else.

Definition

Two moves solve almost everything: convert a log equation to exponential form, or take logs of both sides of an exponential equation.

Worked examples

log₂(x + 3) = 4 → x + 3 = 2⁴ = 16 → x = 13. 2ˣ = 32 → x = log₂ 32 = 5, or take log₁₀ of both sides: x log 2 = log 32 → x = 1.505/0.301 = 5.

Check every root

A solution that makes any argument zero or negative is rejected: log₂(x − 5) = 2 gives x = 9, which is fine, but a computed x = 3 would be rejected because log₂(3 − 5) does not exist. Write the domain condition first, then solve.

Engineering use

pH = −log₁₀[H⁺] and sound level L = 10 log₁₀(I/I₀). A pH of 4 means [H⁺] = 10⁻⁴ mol/L; a 20 dB increase is a hundredfold increase in intensity, not double.

Working

  1. Main diagonal: 5 × 4 = 20
  2. Other diagonal: (−2) × 3 = −6
  3. 20 − (−6) = 26

Answer

26. Subtracting a negative product adds: keep the sign of b with b when you multiply.

Working

  1. x² − 12 = 12
  2. x² = 24
  3. x = √24 = 2√6 ≈ 4.899 or x = −2√6

Answer

x = ±2√6. Both roots satisfy the determinant; leave the answer in surd form unless decimals are asked for.

h.en: Practice 3. Evaluate |3 1 2; 0 4 1; 2 0 5| by expanding along the first column.

body.en:
Working

  1. 3 × (4×5 − 1×0) = 60
  2. −0 × (…) = 0
  3. +2 × (1×1 − 2×4) = 2 × (−7) = −14
  4. 60 + 0 − 14 = 46

Check

Expanding along the first row: 3(20 − 0) − 1(0 − 2) + 2(0 − 8) = 60 + 2 − 16 = 46 ✓ - the value does not depend on the chosen line.

h.en: Practice 4. Find the cofactor of the entry 4 in [1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 9].

body.en:
Working

Position (2, 1) carries a minus sign. Delete row 2 and column 1: the minor is |2 3; 8 9| = 18 − 24 = −6. Cofactor = −(−6) = 6.

Answer

6. Note the determinant of the whole matrix is 0 (row 3 = 2 × row 2 − row 1), which does not stop a single cofactor from being non-zero.

h.en: Practice 5. Solve 3x + 2y = 16, x + y = 6 by Cramer's rule.

body.en:
Working

  1. D = 3(1) − 2(1) = 1
  2. Dx = 16(1) − 2(6) = 4 → x = 4
  3. Dy = 3(6) − 16(1) = 2 → y = 2

Check

3(4) + 2(2) = 16 ✓ and 4 + 2 = 6 ✓. D = 1 makes the division exact, which is a good sign that the coefficients were copied correctly.

h.en: Practice 6. Find the area of the triangle (0, 0), (5, 0), (0, 4).

body.en:
Working

Area = ½|0(0 − 4) + 5(4 − 0) + 0(0 − 0)| = ½|20| = 10.

Answer

10 square units - the familiar right triangle with legs 5 and 4, so ½ × 5 × 4 = 10 confirms it.

h.en: Practice 7. For f(x) = x² + 2x find f(−3) and f(1/2).

body.en:
Working

  1. f(−3) = 9 − 6 = 3
  2. f(1/2) = 1/4 + 1 = 5/4

Answer

3 and 5/4. Bracket every substituted value, especially a fraction: (1/2)² = 1/4, not 1/2.

h.en: Practice 8. Find the domain and range of f(x) = √(4 − x).

body.en:
Working

  1. 4 − x ≥ 0 → x ≤ 4, so the domain is (−∞, 4]
  2. A principal square root is never negative and reaches 0 at x = 4
  3. Range = [0, ∞)

Check

f(4) = 0 and f(0) = 2: outputs start at 0 and grow without limit as x becomes very negative ✓.

h.en: Practice 9. Is f(x) = x⁴ + 2x² even, odd or neither?

body.en:
Working

f(−x) = (−x)⁴ + 2(−x)² = x⁴ + 2x² = f(x), so the function is even.

Answer

Even. Every power of x is even, and that is a quick rule: a polynomial with only even powers is even, only odd powers is odd, mixed is neither.

Working

  1. 3⁴ = 81 → log₃ 81 = 4
  2. 7⁻² = 1/49 → log₇ (1/49) = −2

Answer

4 and −2. A fraction smaller than 1 always gives a negative log (base > 1).

Working

log(5x³) − log(y²) = log 5 + log x³ − log y² = log 5 + 3 log x − 2 log y.

Answer

log 5 + 3 log x − 2 log y. Check by condensing: the terms rebuild log(5x³/y²) exactly.

Working

  1. log 8 + log 125 = log 1000
  2. log 1000 − log 10 = log 100
  3. log 100 = 2

Answer

2. A calculator confirms 0.903 + 2.097 − 1 = 2.000 ✓.

Working

  1. Domain first: x − 1 > 0, so x > 1
  2. Convert to exponential form: x − 1 = 2³ = 8
  3. x = 9

Check

log₂(9 − 1) = log₂ 8 = 3 ✓, and 9 satisfies x > 1. The domain condition is not decoration: without it a computed root such as x = 0 would be accepted wrongly.

h.en: Practice 14. A sound is 1000 times more intense than the threshold I₀. Find its level in dB.

body.en:
Working

  1. L = 10 log₁₀(I/I₀)
  2. = 10 log₁₀ 1000
  3. = 10 × 3 = 30

Answer

30 dB. Each factor of 10 adds 10 dB, so a 1000-fold intensity is 3 × 10 dB - never 1000 dB.

title.en: A function is a one-output machine

terms.en: Main diagonal minus the other diagonal.
Minors are the 2×2 determinants left after deleting a row and a column.
Signs follow the + − + board of the position, not the entry.
Replace the column of the variable being found by the constants.

items.f: ½ |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|

terms.en: Area 0 means the three points are collinear.
One input gives exactly one output; A is the domain, B the codomain.
These three conditions cover every domain question in this unit.
Even is symmetric about the y-axis, odd about the origin.

items.f: ax² + bx + c = a(x + b/2a)² + (c − b²/4a)

terms.en: Reads off the vertex, hence the range of a quadratic.

items.f: y = logₐ x ⇔ aʸ = x, x > 0, a > 0, a ≠ 1

terms.en: A logarithm is an exponent: it answers "what power of a gives x?".

items.f: logₐ(xy) = logₐ x + logₐ y;  logₐ(x/y) = logₐ x − logₐ y

terms.en: Multiplication becomes addition; division becomes subtraction.
Brings the exponent down in front - the workhorse of every log numerical.

items.f: logₐ x = log_b x / log_b a

terms.en: Use base 10 for a calculator, or the common base of the two numbers.

items.f: logₐ 1 = 0, logₐ a = 1, a^(logₐ x) = x

terms.en: Immediate from the definition; useful for simplifying final answers.

q.en: Evaluate the determinant |3 5; 2 4|.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

A second-order determinant: rows (3, 5) and (2, 4).

Formula

|a b; c d| = ad − bc

Step-by-step solution

  1. Main diagonal: 3 × 4 = 12
  2. Other diagonal: 5 × 2 = 10
  3. 12 − 10 = 2

Interpretation and check

2. The determinant is a single number, so the answer must not be written as an array. A quick mental check: 12 is bigger than 10, so the sign is positive.

q.en: Evaluate |−4 7; 3 −2|.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Negative entries - keep each sign with its number.

Formula

ad − bc

Step-by-step solution

  1. a = −4, d = −2 → (−4)(−2) = 8
  2. b = 7, c = 3 → (7)(3) = 21
  3. 8 − 21 = −13

Interpretation and check

−13. Check by expanding along the second row instead: −(3)(7) + (−2)(−4) = −21 + 8 = −13 ✓ - the value is the same whichever row you use.

q.en: Find x if |x 2; 3 x| = 10.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

The entries contain x, so the determinant becomes an equation.

Formula

|x 2; 3 x| = x·x − 2·3

Step-by-step solution

  1. x² − 6 = 10
  2. x² = 16
  3. x = 4 or x = −4

Interpretation and check

x = ±4. Check both: for x = 4 the determinant is 16 − 6 = 10 ✓; for x = −4 it is also 16 − 6 = 10 ✓. Both roots are valid unless the question names a positive x.

q.en: Evaluate |1 2 3; 4 5 6; 7 8 10| by expanding along the first row.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Third-order determinant with the sign pattern + − + along row 1.

Formula

a₁(b₂c₃ − b₃c₂) − b₁(a₂c₃ − a₃c₂) + c₁(a₂b₃ − a₃b₂)

Step-by-step solution

  1. 1 × (5×10 − 6×8) = 1 × 2 = 2
  2. −2 × (4×10 − 6×7) = −2 × (−2) = +4
  3. 3 × (4×8 − 5×7) = 3 × (−3) = −9
  4. 2 + 4 − 9 = −3

Interpretation and check

−3. Sarrus check: (1·5·10 + 2·6·7 + 3·4·8) − (3·5·7 + 1·6·8 + 2·4·10) = (50 + 84 + 96) − (105 + 48 + 80) = 230 − 233 = −3 ✓.

q.en: Evaluate |2 −1 3; 0 4 −2; 5 1 0| using the most convenient line.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Two zeros: entry (2, 1) and entry (3, 3).

Formula

Expand along the third column (entries 3, −2, 0)

Step-by-step solution

  1. 3 × (0×1 − 4×5) = 3 × (−20) = −60
  2. −(−2) × (2×1 − (−1)×5) = +2 × 7 = +14
  3. 0 × (minor) = 0
  4. −60 + 14 + 0 = −46

Interpretation and check

−46. The same answer comes from row 2: −0(...) + 4(2×0 − 3×5) − (−2)(2×1 − (−1)5) = −60 + 14 = −46 ✓. Choosing the line with zeros halves the arithmetic.

q.en: For A = [2 3 1; 4 0 5; 1 2 3] write the cofactor of each entry and find |A|.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Nine minors, each with the positional sign from the + − + board.

Formula

Cᵢⱼ = (−1)^(i+j) Mᵢⱼ

Step-by-step solution

  1. C₁₁ = +(0×3 − 5×2) = −10; C₁₂ = −(4×3 − 5×1) = −7; C₁₃ = +(4×2 − 0×1) = 8
  2. C₂₁ = −(3×3 − 1×2) = −7; C₂₂ = +(2×3 − 1×1) = 5; C₂₃ = −(2×2 − 3×1) = −1
  3. C₃₁ = +(3×5 − 1×0) = 15; C₃₂ = −(2×5 − 1×4) = −6; C₃₃ = +(2×0 − 3×4) = −12
  4. |A| = 2(−10) + 3(−7) + 1(8) = −20 − 21 + 8 = −33

Interpretation and check

|A| = −33. Sarrus: (0 + 15 + 8) − (0 + 36 + 20) = 23 − 56 = −33 ✓. Note that the cofactors are not all positive - the board alternates by position.

q.en: Solve 2x + 3y = 12 and x − y = 1 by Cramer's rule.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Coefficients a₁ = 2, b₁ = 3, c₁ = 12 and a₂ = 1, b₂ = −1, c₂ = 1.

Formula

D = |a₁ b₁; a₂ b₂|, Dx = |c₁ b₁; c₂ b₂|, Dy = |a₁ c₁; a₂ c₂|, x = Dx/D, y = Dy/D

Step-by-step solution

  1. D = (2)(−1) − (3)(1) = −5
  2. Dx = (12)(−1) − (3)(1) = −15, so x = −15/−5 = 3
  3. Dy = (2)(1) − (12)(1) = −10, so y = −10/−5 = 2

Interpretation and check

x = 3, y = 2. Check in the original equations: 2(3) + 3(2) = 12 ✓ and 3 − 2 = 1 ✓. D ≠ 0, so the system has exactly one solution - consistent with the lines crossing once.

q.en: Solve x + y + z = 6, x − y + z = 2, 2x + y − z = 1 by determinants.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Coefficient matrix [1 1 1; 1 −1 1; 2 1 −1]; constants (6, 2, 1).

Formula

D, Dx, Dy, Dz - replace one column of coefficients by the constants each time

Step-by-step solution

  1. D = 1(1 − 1) − 1(−1 − 2) + 1(1 + 2) = 0 + 3 + 3 = 6
  2. Dx = 6(1 − 1) − 1(−2 − 1) + 1(2 + 1) = 0 + 3 + 3 = 6 → x = 1
  3. Dy = 1(−2 − 1) − 6(−1 − 2) + 1(1 − 4) = −3 + 18 − 3 = 12 → y = 2
  4. Dz = 1(−1 − 2) − 1(1 − 4) + 6(1 + 2) = −3 + 3 + 18 = 18 → z = 3

Interpretation and check

x = 1, y = 2, z = 3. Check all three: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 ✓; 1 − 2 + 3 = 2 ✓; 2(1) + 2 − 3 = 1 ✓. D = 6 ≠ 0 guarantees a unique solution.

q.en: Find the area of the triangle with vertices A(1, 2), B(4, 6), C(7, 2).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Three vertices; the base AC is horizontal at y = 2 from x = 1 to x = 7.

Formula

Area = ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|

Step-by-step solution

  1. 1(6 − 2) = 4
  2. 4(2 − 2) = 0
  3. 7(2 − 6) = −28
  4. Area = ½|4 + 0 − 28| = ½ × 24 = 12

Interpretation and check

12 square units. Geometric check: base AC = 7 − 1 = 6 units and the height of B above the base is 6 − 2 = 4 units, so area = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 ✓.

q.en: Show that the points (1, 2), (3, 6) and (5, 10) are collinear.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Collinear points enclose no area, so the determinant form must vanish.

Formula

½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)| = 0 means collinear

Step-by-step solution

  1. 1(6 − 10) = −4
  2. 3(10 − 2) = 24
  3. 5(2 − 6) = −20
  4. −4 + 24 − 20 = 0, so the area is 0

Interpretation and check

Collinear. Confirmation by slope: the slope from (1, 2) to (3, 6) is 4/2 = 2 and from (3, 6) to (5, 10) is also 4/2 = 2, so all three lie on y = 2x.

q.en: For f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1 find f(0), f(2) and f(−1).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Substitute each value in brackets and apply BODMAS.

Formula

Replace x by the given number everywhere

Step-by-step solution

  1. f(0) = 0 − 0 + 1 = 1
  2. f(2) = 2(4) − 6 + 1 = 3
  3. f(−1) = 2(1) + 3 + 1 = 6

Interpretation and check

1, 3 and 6. Check f(2) by factorising the answer: 2x² − 3x + 1 = (2x − 1)(x − 1), so f(2) = (3)(1) = 3 ✓. The bracket rule saves the sign in f(−1).

q.en: Find the domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 3) and of g(x) = √(x − 2).

a.en:
Given and assumptions

A denominator must not be zero; a square root must not be negative.

Formula

denominator ≠ 0, radicand ≥ 0

Step-by-step solution

  1. x − 3 ≠ 0 → x ≠ 3, so the domain of f is all real x except 3
  2. x − 2 ≥ 0 → x ≥ 2, so the domain of g is [2, ∞)

Interpretation and check

R − {3} and [2, ∞). Test one value outside each answer: f(3) is undefined, and g(1) = √(−1) is not real ✓. Write the domain as a set or an interval, never as a word.

q.en: Find the domain and range of f(x) = x² − 4x + 7.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

A quadratic; complete the square to read the vertex.

Formula

x² + bx + c = (x + b/2)² + c − b²/4

Step-by-step solution

  1. x² − 4x + 7 = (x − 2)² + 3
  2. Domain: every real x, because a polynomial has no restriction
  3. Range: (x − 2)² ≥ 0, so f(x) ≥ 3

Interpretation and check

Domain R, range [3, ∞), vertex (2, 3). Check f(2) = 4 − 8 + 7 = 3, and f(0) = 7 ≥ 3 ✓. The bracket (x − 2)² can never be negative, which is why 3 is the minimum.

q.en: Evaluate the piecewise function f(x) = x + 1 for x < 0 and f(x) = x² for x ≥ 0 at x = −2, 0 and 3.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

The rule is chosen by the input, and the boundary value x = 0 belongs to the second rule because it is written x ≥ 0.

Formula

Use the branch whose condition the input satisfies

Step-by-step solution

  1. x = −2 < 0, so f(−2) = −2 + 1 = −1
  2. x = 0 ≥ 0, so f(0) = 0² = 0
  3. x = 3 ≥ 0, so f(3) = 3² = 9

Interpretation and check

−1, 0 and 9. Each output is a single number - if you get two answers for one input, the branches overlap and the relation is not a function at that point.

q.en: Test whether f(x) = x³ − x is even, odd or neither; then test g(x) = x² + x.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Replace x by −x and compare.

Formula

Even: f(−x) = f(x); odd: f(−x) = −f(x)

Step-by-step solution

  1. f(−x) = (−x)³ − (−x) = −x³ + x = −(x³ − x) = −f(x) → odd
  2. g(−x) = (−x)² + (−x) = x² − x
  3. x² − x is neither g(x) = x² + x nor −g(x) = −x² − x → neither

Interpretation and check

f is odd, g is neither. Check numerically: f(2) = 6 and f(−2) = −6 (opposite ✓); g(2) = 6 but g(−2) = 2, which is neither 6 nor −6 ✓.

q.en: Evaluate log₂ 32, log₃ (1/27), log₁₀ 1000 and log₅ 1.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Use the definition: logₐ x is the power that turns a into x.

Formula

y = logₐ x ⇔ aʸ = x

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2⁵ = 32 → log₂ 32 = 5
  2. 3⁻³ = 1/27 → log₃ (1/27) = −3
  3. 10³ = 1000 → log₁₀ 1000 = 3
  4. 5⁰ = 1 → log₅ 1 = 0

Interpretation and check

5, −3, 3 and 0. Two sanity rules cover all four: logₐ 1 = 0 always, and a logarithm is negative exactly when the argument is below 1 (for base > 1).

q.en: Find a if logₐ 8 = 3/2.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

An unknown base; convert to exponential form.

Formula

logₐ x = y ⇔ aʸ = x

Step-by-step solution

  1. a^(3/2) = 8
  2. Square both sides: a³ = 64
  3. a = 4

Interpretation and check

a = 4. Check: 4^(3/2) = (√4)³ = 2³ = 8 ✓. The base must be positive and not 1 - 4 satisfies both.

q.en: Expand log(3x²/y) using the laws of logarithm.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

All arguments are positive (x > 0, y > 0), so every law applies.

Formula

log(xy) = log x + log y; log(x/y) = log x − log y; log xⁿ = n log x

Step-by-step solution

  1. log(3x²) − log y (quotient law)
  2. log 3 + log x² − log y (product law)
  3. log 3 + 2 log x − log y (power law)

Interpretation and check

log 3 + 2 log x − log y. Combine it back: log 3 + log x² − log y = log(3x²/y) ✓. The number of terms in the answer equals the number of factors in the argument.

q.en: Write 2 log 3 + log 4 − log 6 as a single logarithm.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Condensing is the reverse of the expansion.

Formula

n log x = log xⁿ, then product and quotient laws

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2 log 3 = log 9
  2. log 9 + log 4 = log 36
  3. log 36 − log 6 = log 6

Interpretation and check

log 6. Numerically: 2(0.4771) + 0.6021 − 0.7782 = 0.7781 ≈ log 6 = 0.7782 ✓ (the tiny gap is rounding in the tables).

q.en: Given log 2 = 0.3010 and log 3 = 0.4771, find log 72.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

72 is not in the tables, so break it into primes: 72 = 8 × 9 = 2³ × 3².

Formula

log(xy) = log x + log y and log xⁿ = n log x

Step-by-step solution

  1. log 72 = log(2³ × 3²)
  2. = 3 log 2 + 2 log 3
  3. = 3(0.3010) + 2(0.4771)
  4. = 0.9030 + 0.9542 = 1.8572

Interpretation and check

1.8572. Check the size: 72 lies between 10 and 100, so log 72 must lie between 1 and 2 ✓. A result outside that range means a slip in the table values.

q.en: Evaluate log₄ 8 without a calculator.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Both numbers are powers of 2.

Formula

logₐ x = log_b x / log_b a

Step-by-step solution

  1. log₄ 8 = log₂ 8 / log₂ 4
  2. = 3 / 2
  3. = 1.5

Interpretation and check

3/2. Check by the definition: 4^(3/2) = (√4)³ = 8 ✓. Choosing the common base 2 made the division exact - always look for a shared base before reaching for a calculator.

q.en: Solve 2ˣ = 32 and log₂(x + 3) = 4.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

One exponential equation and one logarithmic equation, both base 2.

Formula

Take logarithms of both sides; or convert log form to exponential form

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2ˣ = 32 = 2⁵ → x = 5
  2. log₂(x + 3) = 4 → x + 3 = 2⁴ = 16
  3. x = 13

Interpretation and check

x = 5 and x = 13. Check: 2⁵ = 32 ✓ and log₂(13 + 3) = log₂ 16 = 4 ✓. The argument 13 + 3 = 16 is positive, so no rejection is needed.

q.en: Find the pH of a solution with hydrogen-ion concentration [H⁺] = 1 × 10⁻⁴ mol/L.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

pH = −log₁₀[H⁺].

Formula

pH = −log₁₀[H⁺]

Step-by-step solution

  1. pH = −log₁₀(10⁻⁴)
  2. log₁₀(10⁻⁴) = −4
  3. pH = −(−4) = 4

Interpretation and check

pH = 4, an acidic solution (below 7). A tenfold increase in [H⁺] lowers the pH by exactly 1, because each decade is one unit on a logarithmic scale.

q.en: A bacterial culture doubles every 20 minutes. Starting with 1000 bacteria, when will it reach 8000?

a.en:
Given and assumptions

Growth by a fixed factor, so the count after t minutes is 1000 × 2^(t/20).

Formula

1000 × 2^(t/20) = 8000

Step-by-step solution

  1. 2^(t/20) = 8
  2. 2^(t/20) = 2³
  3. t/20 = 3
  4. t = 60 minutes = 1 hour

Interpretation and check

60 minutes. Check by counting doublings: 1000 → 2000 (20 min) → 4000 (40 min) → 8000 (60 min) ✓. With logs: t = 20 log₂ 8 = 20 × 3 = 60.

q.en: Show that log₂ 8 × log₈ 2 = 1, and state the general result.

a.en:
Given and assumptions

log₂ 8 = 3 and log₈ 2 is the same question reversed.

Formula

logₐ b = 1 / log_b a

Step-by-step solution

  1. log₂ 8 = 3
  2. log₈ 2 = 1/3, because 8^(1/3) = 2
  3. Product = 3 × 1/3 = 1

Interpretation and check

1. General rule: logₐ b · log_b a = 1 for any valid bases. It is the change-of-base formula with the two bases swapped, and it turns "evaluate in another base" questions into one division.

q.en: What is a determinant?

a.en: A single number calculated from a square array of numbers, written with vertical bars.

q.en: State the value of a 2×2 determinant.

a.en: ad − bc: the product of the main diagonal minus the product of the other diagonal.

q.en: What is the minor of an entry?

a.en: The determinant left after deleting the row and the column containing that entry.

q.en: How does a cofactor differ from a minor?

a.en: The cofactor adds the positional sign: Cᵢⱼ = (−1)^(i+j) Mᵢⱼ.

q.en: Which row should you choose to expand a third-order determinant?

a.en: The one with the most zeros, because each zero removes a whole 2×2 determinant.

q.en: If D = 0 in Cramer's rule, what can you say?

a.en: Either there is no solution (parallel lines) or there are infinitely many (the same line); Dx and Dy decide which.

q.en: How do you test whether three points are collinear?

a.en: The area formula must give zero, that is the determinant of the three points is zero.

q.en: Define a function.

a.en: A rule that assigns exactly one element of the codomain to every element of the domain.

q.en: What is the domain of 1/(x − 3)?

a.en: All real numbers except 3, because the denominator must not be zero.

q.en: What is the domain of √(x − 2)?

a.en: x ≥ 2, because a square root of a negative number is not real.

q.en: When is a function even?

a.en: When f(−x) = f(x) for every x in the domain; its graph is symmetric about the y-axis.

q.en: When is a function odd?

a.en: When f(−x) = −f(x) for every x; its graph is symmetric about the origin.

q.en: What is the range of a quadratic with a positive leading coefficient?

a.en: From the vertex's y-value upward, y ≥ k, because the parabola opens upward.

q.en: What does the vertical line test check?

a.en: That no vertical line meets the graph twice, which means each input has only one output.

q.en: Define logₐ x.

a.en: The exponent to which a must be raised to get x: y = logₐ x ⇔ aʸ = x.

q.en: What is the domain of a logarithm?

a.en: x > 0, because no power of a positive base gives zero or a negative number.

q.en: State the product law.

a.en: logₐ(xy) = logₐ x + logₐ y.

q.en: State the quotient law.

a.en: logₐ(x/y) = logₐ x − logₐ y.

q.en: State the power law.

a.en: logₐ(xⁿ) = n logₐ x.

q.en: How do you change the base of a logarithm?

a.en: logₐ x = log_b x / log_b a, for any valid new base b.

q.en: What are logₐ 1 and logₐ a?

a.en: logₐ 1 = 0 and logₐ a = 1, for every valid base a.

q.en: Is log(x + y) equal to log x + log y?

a.en: No. The product law applies to log(xy); a sum inside a logarithm cannot be split.

q.en: Why is a 20 dB increase a hundredfold, not a doubling?

a.en: Sound level uses 10 log₁₀; +20 dB means the ratio grew by 10² = 100.
